newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo needs $900 million for 1997 energy imports.
newsitem.headline: Yugo needs $900 million for 1997 energy imports.

text.p: Yugoslavia will need around $900 million for 1997 energy imports to meet an expected 11 percent increase in domestic energy demand, Belgrade media reported on Thursday.

According to the Yugoslav government 1997 draft energy balance, the country would need to import $430 million worth of crude, $130 million of derivatives, $265 million of gas, $75 million of coke and $12 million of brown coal, the Belgrade newspaper Politika said.
Most of the quantities will come from barter deals with China and Russia, the paper said.
The 1997 energy balance assumes domestic electricity production of 37,109 GigaWatt-hours (GWh) while demand is estimated at 37,882 GWh.
Local coal production and consumption are expected to be balanced and were seen at around 41 million tonnes or 5.8 percent up on 1996.
